name: Resting Hardtooth
description: Both hands take the haft and the feet plant wide, so the shaft covers the chest while the pick head hangs ready.

name: Drive Drop
description: The pick lifts above the shoulder and the spike drops straight down onto the target with the whole body behind it.

name: Crackdrop
description: The wrist turns the pick so the blunt face raps the target sharply in a short arc, without a full swing.

name: Raised Crowbill
description: Held crosswise in both hands, the haft catches an incoming blow on its wood and turns it aside.

name: Peckhead Amble
description: The rear foot slides back along the ground to open distance after a strike while the pick head stays forward.

name: Turning Puncture
description: The curved beak catches behind a shield rim or sleeve and tugs, dragging the target's balance forward.

name: Chinkstrike
description: Short repeated taps of the spike against one mark on a post train a straight, certain path for the pick head.

name: Spikebeak Pause
description: The pick stands upright before the body at shoulder width, so haft and head together screen the torso.

name: Nabbing Chink
description: A twist of the haft and a hard pull wrench a sunk spike loose, jerking the held target off balance.

name: Stepping Pickhelve
description: Small flat-footed steps carry the student forward with the pick held low, keeping the spike on its target line.

name: Soft Pickfluke
description: A light rap of the haft on armor and a listening ear tell the hollow ring of thin metal from the solid ring.

name: Pickbump
description: The flat hammer face swings level against the side of a helmet and jars the wearer's skull inside it.

name: Level Punch
description: Both hands push the beak forward in a short jab at a gap in cloth or leather.

name: Planted Waistpoint
description: The lower hand slides up the haft to shorten the lever, keeping the heavy head close and the chest covered.

name: Settled Ironthorn
description: The pick rises from low guard and the broad hammer face meets an arm or blade, knocking it wide.

name: Wide Stonetip
description: The haft slides through the rear hand to add a forearm of reach, and the beak stabs one extra length.

name: Picktrot
description: A step off the line to the side lets the hammer face come back on the return swing against the ribs.

name: Soft Backbill
description: One quick look over the target's armor decides whether the blunt face or the pointed beak will serve.

name: Peck Bump
description: The lead foot drives forward and carries the beak into the target in one long lunge.

name: Blunt Pickhelve
description: A turn of the hips whips the hammer face around in a flat arc, so the blow comes from the legs.

name: Crackpace
description: The rear foot crosses behind the lead one while the haft stays level, closing distance without lifting the pick.

name: Nimble Pickfluke
description: A pivot on the ball of the lead foot swings the body off the line of an incoming thrust.

name: Pickstay
description: Knees bend and tendons lock so the body bears a shove through the haft without giving ground.

name: Stopping Crowbill
description: The beak hooks over a shield rim and the student hauls back, pulling the shield down and open.

name: Towing Spikebeak
description: The beak snags a sleeve or strap and holds it taut, so the target cannot freely raise that arm.

name: Drivecowl
description: The beak sweeps low behind an ankle and draws back, tipping a standing opponent onto his back.

name: Light Peck
description: When a hooked target pulls against the haft, one quick backstep gives slack and frees the beak.

name: Hooding Stonetip
description: The beak turns upward to crook an incoming haft or blade and ride it harmlessly aside.

name: Wide Backbill
description: Right after a hooking pull, the hammer face drives into the staggered target at close range.

name: Hooding Peckhead
description: A thread of qi runs from both palms into the haft, firming the grip and the guard held behind it.

name: Crowblow
description: A little qi gathers in the pick head as it falls, so the spike bites a hand deeper than a plain drop.

name: Upward Crack
description: A short qi pulse leaves the hammer face as it lands, adding a sharp jolt to a plain rap.

name: Tight Waistpoint
description: Qi stiffens the haft so a blade lands on it with a ringing note and slides off the wood.

name: Stepping Puncture
description: A puff of qi in the soles lets the student skip one pace sideways, light and fast, with the pick held ready.

name: Stopping Chink
description: Qi tightens the beak's catch on a rim or strap, and the sharp haul tears the hold from the target's grasp.

name: Pickcount
description: A faint qi pulse down the haft lets the hand feel through the head whether the target's armor is sound or worn.

name: Pickgauge
description: A slow breath lets the qi settle through the haft into steady hands before the next stroke.

name: Tending Crowbill
description: The eye traces a clear line from the student's gaze to the chosen mark and the spike falls into line.

name: Gnawing Ironthorn
description: The pick advances in a slow, breath-timed push that seats the spike exactly on the chosen mark.

name: Crowhusk
description: Qi sinks to the lower belly and the pick holds a still, upright guard before the body.

name: Shifting Pickhelve
description: A half step to either side brings a drifting pick point back onto its mark before the thrust lands.

name: Crackhusk
description: The beak nudges into the edge of an armor seam and twists, prying two plates slightly apart.

name: Narrow Drive
description: The qi-fed spike drives between the links of a mail coat and spreads them, reaching the padding below.

name: Short Chink
description: The point finds the narrow gap between plates at the elbow and pokes through the opening.

name: Descending Crack
description: The hammer face lands flat on a breastplate and dents it inward, driving the breath out of the wearer.

name: Settled Pickfluke
description: The haft rises at a slant under qi and meets a descending sword cut, turning the edge off the student.

name: Crowcowl
description: The student crouches behind the pick held high, so the head and haft cover helm and shoulders from above.

name: Drivepace
description: Short qi-aided shuffles keep the student chest to chest with an armored foe, inside the sweep of his weapon.

name: Kind Spikebeak
description: A glance along straps, buckles and rivets shows where the armor fits poorly and where the pick should go.

name: Hardtooth Husk
description: The student lets the pick head's weight hang from the haft, holding a low guard that costs no strain.

name: Crowstrike
description: Gripped at the butt, the haft gives full length, and the spike reaches farthest in one straight thrust.

name: Gnawing Waistpoint
description: With the hand choked near the head, the pick whips a quick hammer blow where a long swing would not fit.

name: Hardtooth Lid
description: After a miss the lead hand slides down the haft and drags the head home before a counter arrives.

name: Light Puncture
description: The feet follow the falling weight of the head, so each stroke ends with the student balanced and square.

name: Pickhit
description: The pick reverses and the butt end of the haft jabs into the target's midsection at close range.

name: Lowered Stonetip
description: Held upright and close, the pick guards the face and throat while bodies crowd against the student on both sides.

name: Hitching Crack
description: The beak hooks over an enemy's shoulder strap in a crowd and hauls him out of his rank.

name: Flukehit
description: With no room to swing, a short stab of the spike goes through a gap between two shields.

name: Drive Dodge
description: The student edges sideways through a packed line, planting each foot before shifting weight.

name: Crowreview
description: A probing toe tests the footing before a swing, so wet or rutted ground does not spoil the stroke.
